chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Najran and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding two sisters: a man married one, then divorced her while she was pregnant, then proposed to the other, and united them (in marriage) before the divorced sister gave birth to her child. He ordered him to separate from the second sister until the divorced sister gave birth to her child, then he should propose to her and pay her dowry twice.
And whenever a man marries two sisters in a single contract, he may keep whichever he wishes and release the other.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on marrying two sisters if one is divorced while pregnant?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the application of *al-Khita'ayn* (two sisters) by distinguishing between simultaneous marriage and sequential marriage with an intervening period. It establishes that a man must separate from the second sister until the first sister completes her *Iddah* (waiting period), which extends through childbirth in this case, ensuring the prohibition is fully observed. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the precise timing of the *Iddah* as the condition for the validity of marrying the second sister.
